text:
kai: Heads-up — seeing p95 east->west latency spikes between GPU nodes in cluster-e during the noon batching window (12:05–12:20). kv-cache hitrate dropped 92% -> ~40%. tails hitting 180–220ms, some retransmits seen.
sarah: Any recent MTU or kernel changes rolled to cluster-e?
mike-net: I picked up RDMA negotiation fallbacks on a subset: gnode-07/08/21 fell back to TCP. dmesg shows: ```psm2: negotiation failed, falling back to sockets```
jen: The infra patch that adjusted qdisc settings landed last night but it was scoped to only a few racks. not the whole cluster.
ops-bot: ALERT: batch-window-latency | cluster-e | p95 185ms | window 12:06-12:14 | triggered at 1719502508 :rotating_light:
alex-rt: kv-cache eviction rate spikes too? if cache thrashed, prefix caching warmup would force more remote fetches across the fabric. can you paste `kvcache-stats` from an impacted node?
kai: attaching quick snippets from gnode-07: ```kvcache_hits: 4123
kvcache_misses: 6204
evictions/sec: 48
net-retrans: 137```
mike-net: tcpdump on the peerlink shows increased out-of-order + retrans at same interval. sample: ```12:07:13.123 IP 10.1.7.21.60000 > 10.1.7.22.45000: seq 12345 ack 67890 (retransmission)```
sarah: Could MTU mismatch be causing fragmentation on the east-west path? anyone see PMTU logs?
mike-net: Good call — interface stats show occasional 'frag_dropped' on the ToR facing the cluster spine. Also tor team reported an auto-MTU negotiation event at 11:58.
jen: Ops rolled a minor MTU tweak to the tenant fabric at 11:59 to unify jumbo frames for a different rack. I didn't realize cluster-e would traverse that path.
alex-rt: So a plausible chain: MTU tweak -> intermittent fragmentation -> RDMA negotiation fallback -> more TCP flows -> kv-cache misses amplify east-west fetches -> spike in p95.
kai: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: 1) pin hot-serving pods to nodes that don't traverse the changed ToR (zone-aware scheduling), 2) add a temporary routing rule to prefer alternate spine for cluster-e, 3) rollback MTU tweak if quick fix needed.
mike-net: I'll open a tor rollback ticket and run a controlled rollback in the affected rack. Will also force RDMA re-negotiate after rollback.
ops-bot: ACTION CREATED: #INC-2026-1874 opened by mike-net — tor-mtu-rollback for rack 17.
sarah: For postmortem, let's capture kvcache traffic patterns and correlate with RDMA/TCP fallback windows. also add a small synthetic traffic run during next noon window to validate.
kai: Thanks — i'll coordinate the canary workload and update this thread when rollback complete or if we need an emergency rollback. :thumbsup:
